Waffen-SS.question: That same day, as the SS _____ advanced near Merville, they encountered stubborn resistance from British Army units, which slowed their advance
Waffen-SS.fact: That same day, as the SS Totenkopf Division advanced near Merville, they encountered stubborn resistance from British Army units, which slowed their advance.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: By 28 May, the _____ had taken the village of Wormhout, only ten miles from Dunkirk
Waffen-SS.fact: By 28 May, the Leibstandarte had taken the village of Wormhout, only ten miles from Dunkirk. It was there that troops of the Leibstandarte's 2nd Battalion committed the Wormhoudt massacre, where 81 British and French prisoners of war were murdered.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: It was there that troops of the _____'s 2nd Battalion committed the Wormhoudt massacre, where 81 British and French prisoners of war were murdered
Waffen-SS.fact: By 28 May, the Leibstandarte had taken the village of Wormhout, only ten miles from Dunkirk. It was there that troops of the Leibstandarte's 2nd Battalion committed the Wormhoudt massacre, where 81 British and French prisoners of war were murdered.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: After their surrender, soldiers from the 2nd Battalion, _____, along with some other units (including French soldiers), were taken to a barn in La Plaine au Bois near Wormhout and Esquelbecq
Waffen-SS.fact: After their surrender, soldiers from the 2nd Battalion, Royal Warwickshire Regiment, along with some other units (including French soldiers), were taken to a barn in La Plaine au Bois near Wormhout and Esquelbecq.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: By 30 May, the _____ were cornered at Dunkirk, and the SS divisions continued the advance into France
Waffen-SS.fact: It was there that troops of the Leibstandarte's 2nd Battalion committed the Wormhoudt massacre, where 81 British and French prisoners of war were murdered. By 30 May, the British were cornered at Dunkirk, and the SS divisions continued the advance into France.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: The Leibstandarte reached Saint-Étienne, _____ south of Paris, and had advanced further into France than any other unit
Waffen-SS.fact: The Leibstandarte reached Saint-Étienne, 250 miles south of Paris, and had advanced further into France than any other unit.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: German forces arrived in Paris unopposed on 14 June and _____ formally surrendered on 25 June
Waffen-SS.fact: By 30 May, the British were cornered at Dunkirk, and the SS divisions continued the advance into France. The Leibstandarte reached Saint-Étienne, 250 miles south of Paris, and had advanced further into France than any other unit.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: Himmler gained approval for the Waffen-SS to form its own high command, the Kommandoamt der Waffen-SS within the SS Führungshauptamt, which was created in August _____
Waffen-SS.fact: Himmler gained approval for the Waffen-SS to form its own high command, the Kommandoamt der Waffen-SS within the SS Führungshauptamt, which was created in August 1940. In 1940, SS chief of staff Gottlob Berger approached Himmler with a plan to recruit volunteers in the conquered territories from the ethnic German and Germanic populations.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: In _____, SS chief of staff Gottlob Berger approached Himmler with a plan to recruit volunteers in the conquered territories from the ethnic German and Germanic populations
Waffen-SS.fact: Himmler gained approval for the Waffen-SS to form its own high command, the Kommandoamt der Waffen-SS within the SS Führungshauptamt, which was created in August 1940. In 1940, SS chief of staff Gottlob Berger approached Himmler with a plan to recruit volunteers in the conquered territories from the ethnic German and Germanic populations.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: It received command of the SS-VT (the _____ and the Verfügungs-Division, renamed Reich) and the armed SS-TV regiments (the Totenkopf Division together with several independent Totenkopf-Standarten)
Waffen-SS.fact: It received command of the SS-VT (the Leibstandarte and the Verfügungs-Division, renamed Reich) and the armed SS-TV regiments (the Totenkopf Division together with several independent Totenkopf-Standarten).

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: At first, _____ had doubts about recruiting foreigners, but he was persuaded by Himmler and Berger
Waffen-SS.fact: At first, Hitler had doubts about recruiting foreigners, but he was persuaded by Himmler and Berger.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: He gave approval for a new division to be formed from foreign nationals with _____ officers
Waffen-SS.fact: In 1940, SS chief of staff Gottlob Berger approached Himmler with a plan to recruit volunteers in the conquered territories from the ethnic German and Germanic populations. He gave approval for a new division to be formed from foreign nationals with German officers.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: By June _____, Danish and Norwegian volunteers had formed the SS Regiment Nordland, with Dutch and Flemish volunteers forming the SS Regiment Westland
Waffen-SS.fact: In 1940, SS chief of staff Gottlob Berger approached Himmler with a plan to recruit volunteers in the conquered territories from the ethnic German and Germanic populations. By June 1940, Danish and Norwegian volunteers had formed the SS Regiment Nordland, with Dutch and Flemish volunteers forming the SS Regiment Westland.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: The two regiments, together with _____ (transferred from the Reich Division), formed the SS Division Wiking
Waffen-SS.fact: The two regiments, together with Germania (transferred from the Reich Division), formed the SS Division Wiking. The 11th Regiment was transferred into the Reich Division to replace Germania; the remainder were grouped into three independent brigades and a battle group in Norway.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: A sufficient number of volunteers came forward requiring the SS to open a new training camp just for foreign volunteers at _____ in Alsace-Lorraine
Waffen-SS.fact: A sufficient number of volunteers came forward requiring the SS to open a new training camp just for foreign volunteers at Sennheim in Alsace-Lorraine.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: The 11th _____ was transferred into the Reich Division to replace Germania; the remainder were grouped into three independent brigades and a battle group in Norway
Waffen-SS.fact: The two regiments, together with Germania (transferred from the Reich Division), formed the SS Division Wiking. At the same time, the Totenkopf-Standarten, aside from the three constituting the TK-Division, lost their Death's Head designation and insignia and were reclassified SS-Infanterie- (or Kavallerie-) Regimente.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: Operation Marita began on 6 April _____, with German troops invading Greece through Bulgaria and Yugoslavia in an effort to secure its southern flank
Waffen-SS.fact: By spring of 1941, the Waffen-SS consisted of the equivalent of six or seven divisions: the Reich, Totenkopf, Polizei, and Wiking Divisions and Kampfgruppe (later Division) Nord, the Leibstandarte, the 1st SS Infantry, 2nd SS Infantry and SS Cavalry Brigades. Operation Marita began on 6 April 1941, with German troops invading Greece through Bulgaria and Yugoslavia in an effort to secure its southern flank.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: Reich was ordered to leave _____ and head for Romania, and the Leibstandarte was ordered to Bulgaria
Waffen-SS.fact: Reich was ordered to leave France and head for Romania, and the Leibstandarte was ordered to Bulgaria.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: The Leibstandarte, attached to the XL Panzer Corps, advanced west then south from Bulgaria into the mountains, and by 9 April had reached Prilep in Yugoslavia, _____ from the Greek border
Waffen-SS.fact: The Leibstandarte, attached to the XL Panzer Corps, advanced west then south from Bulgaria into the mountains, and by 9 April had reached Prilep in Yugoslavia, 30 miles from the Greek border.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: Further north the _____, with the XLI Panzer Corps, crossed the Romanian border and advanced on Belgrade, the Yugoslav capital
Waffen-SS.fact: Further north the Reich Division, with the XLI Panzer Corps, crossed the Romanian border and advanced on Belgrade, the Yugoslav capital.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: Fritz Klingenberg, a company commander in the Reich, led his men into _____, where a small group in the vanguard accepted the surrender of the city on 13 April
Waffen-SS.fact: Further north the Reich Division, with the XLI Panzer Corps, crossed the Romanian border and advanced on Belgrade, the Yugoslav capital. Fritz Klingenberg, a company commander in the Reich, led his men into Belgrade, where a small group in the vanguard accepted the surrender of the city on 13 April.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: A few days later the _____ surrendered
Waffen-SS.fact: A few days later the Royal Yugoslav Army surrendered.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: The Leibstandarte had now crossed into Greece, and on 10 April engaged the 6th _____ in the Battle of the Klidi Pass
Waffen-SS.fact: The Leibstandarte had now crossed into Greece, and on 10 April engaged the 6th Australian Division in the Battle of the Klidi Pass.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: The next day, Meyer captured _____ and took another 11,000 prisoners of war
Waffen-SS.fact: The next day, Meyer captured Kastoria and took another 11,000 prisoners of war.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: By 20 May, the _____ had cut off the retreating Greek Army at Metsovo and accepted the surrender of the Greek Epirus-Macedonian Army
Waffen-SS.fact: This victory gained praise from the OKW: in the order of the day they were commended for their "unshakable offensive spirit" and told that "the present victory signifies for the Leibstandarte a new and imperishable page of honour in its history." The Leibstandarte continued the advance on 13 May. By 20 May, the Leibstandarte had cut off the retreating Greek Army at Metsovo and accepted the surrender of the Greek Epirus-Macedonian Army.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: By the end of _____, Nord had suffered severe casualties
Waffen-SS.fact: By the end of 1941, Nord had suffered severe casualties. Over the winter of 1941–42 it received replacements from the general pool of Waffen-SS recruits, who were supposedly younger and better trained than the SS men of the original formation, which had been drawn largely from Totenkopfstandarten of Nazi concentration camp guards.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: The Totenkopf and _____ divisions were attached to Army Group North, with the mission to advance through the Baltic states and on to Leningrad
Waffen-SS.fact: The Totenkopf and Polizei divisions were attached to Army Group North, with the mission to advance through the Baltic states and on to Leningrad.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: The Das Reich Division was with _____ and headed towards Moscow
Waffen-SS.fact: The Das Reich Division was with Army Group Centre and headed towards Moscow.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: The Leibstandarte and _____ were with Army Group South, heading for Ukraine and the city of Kiev
Waffen-SS.fact: The Leibstandarte and Wiking Divisions were with Army Group South, heading for Ukraine and the city of Kiev.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: Das Reich lost _____ of its strength and was still to take part in the Battle of Moscow
Waffen-SS.fact: Das Reich lost 60% of its strength and was still to take part in the Battle of Moscow.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: The unit was later decimated in the following _____ offensive
Waffen-SS.fact: The invasion of the Soviet Union proceeded well at first, but the cost to the Waffen-SS was extreme: by late October, the Leibstandarte was at half strength due to enemy action and dysentery that swept through the ranks. The unit was later decimated in the following Soviet offensive.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: The Der Führer _____ was reduced to 35 men out of the 2,000 that had started the campaign in June
Waffen-SS.fact: The Der Führer Regiment was reduced to 35 men out of the 2,000 that had started the campaign in June.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: While the _____ and the SS divisions were fighting in the front line, behind the lines it was a different story
Waffen-SS.fact: While the Leibstandarte and the SS divisions were fighting in the front line, behind the lines it was a different story.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: The 1st SS Infantry and 2nd SS _____, which had been formed from surplus concentration camp guards of the SS-TV, and the SS Cavalry Brigade moved into the Soviet Union behind the advancing armies
Waffen-SS.fact: The 1st SS Infantry and 2nd SS Infantry Brigades, which had been formed from surplus concentration camp guards of the SS-TV, and the SS Cavalry Brigade moved into the Soviet Union behind the advancing armies.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: In the autumn of _____, they left the anti-partisan role to other units and actively took part in the Holocaust
Waffen-SS.fact: At first, they fought Soviet partisans and cut off units of the Red Army in the rear of Army Group South, capturing 7,000 prisoners of war, but from mid-August 1941 until late 1942 they were assigned to the Reich Security Main Office headed by Reinhard Heydrich. In the autumn of 1941, they left the anti-partisan role to other units and actively took part in the Holocaust.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: While assisting the _____, they participated in the extermination of the Jewish population of the Soviet Union, forming firing parties when required
Waffen-SS.fact: While assisting the Einsatzgruppen, they participated in the extermination of the Jewish population of the Soviet Union, forming firing parties when required.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: The three brigades were responsible for the murder of tens of thousands by the end of _____
Waffen-SS.fact: In the autumn of 1941, they left the anti-partisan role to other units and actively took part in the Holocaust. The three brigades were responsible for the murder of tens of thousands by the end of 1941.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: In the summer of _____, Himmler assigned Hermann Fegelein to be in charge of both regiments
Waffen-SS.fact: The three brigades were responsible for the murder of tens of thousands by the end of 1941. In the summer of 1941, Himmler assigned Hermann Fegelein to be in charge of both regiments.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: Fegelein split the territory to be covered into two sections divided by the _____, with the 1st Regiment taking the northern half and the 2nd Regiment the south
Waffen-SS.fact: Fegelein split the territory to be covered into two sections divided by the Pripyat River, with the 1st Regiment taking the northern half and the 2nd Regiment the south.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: By 1 August, 1st SS _____ under the command of Gustav Lombard was responsible for the death of 800 people; by 6 August, this total had reached 3,000 "Jews and partisans"
Waffen-SS.fact: By 1 August, 1st SS Cavalry Regiment under the command of Gustav Lombard was responsible for the death of 800 people; by 6 August, this total had reached 3,000 "Jews and partisans".

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: Throughout the following weeks, the regiment's personnel under _____'s command murdered an estimated 11,000 Jews and more than 400 dispersed soldiers of the Red Army
Waffen-SS.fact: By 1 August, 1st SS Cavalry Regiment under the command of Gustav Lombard was responsible for the death of 800 people; by 6 August, this total had reached 3,000 "Jews and partisans". Throughout the following weeks, the regiment's personnel under Lombard's command murdered an estimated 11,000 Jews and more than 400 dispersed soldiers of the Red Army.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: Fegelein's final operational report dated 18 September _____, states that they killed 14,178 Jews, 1,001 partisans, 699 Red Army soldiers, with 830 prisoners taken and losses of 17 dead, 36 wounded, a
Waffen-SS.fact: Fegelein's final operational report dated 18 September 1941, states that they killed 14,178 Jews, 1,001 partisans, 699 Red Army soldiers, with 830 prisoners taken and losses of 17 dead, 36 wounded, and 3 missing.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: By the second half of _____, an increasing number of foreigners, many of whom were not volunteers, began entering the ranks
Waffen-SS.fact: By the second half of 1942, an increasing number of foreigners, many of whom were not volunteers, began entering the ranks.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: Himmler approved the introduction of formal compulsory service for the _____ in German-occupied Serbia
Waffen-SS.fact: The 7th SS Volunteer Mountain Division Prinz Eugen was recruited from Volksdeutsche (ethnic Germans) drafted under threat of punishment by the local German leadership from Croatia, Serbia, Hungary, and Romania and used for anti-partisan operations in the Balkans. Himmler approved the introduction of formal compulsory service for the Volksdeutsche in German-occupied Serbia.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: Another new division was formed at the same time, when the SS _____ was used as the cadre in the formation of the 8th SS Cavalry Division Florian Geyer
Waffen-SS.fact: Another new division was formed at the same time, when the SS Cavalry Brigade was used as the cadre in the formation of the 8th SS Cavalry Division Florian Geyer.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: They each received nine _____ tanks, which were formed into the heavy panzer companies
Waffen-SS.fact: They each received nine Tiger tanks, which were formed into the heavy panzer companies.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: The Red Army liberated Demyansk on 1 March _____ with the retreat of German troops
Waffen-SS.fact: The Red Army liberated Demyansk on 1 March 1943 with the retreat of German troops.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: "For his excellence in command and the particularly fierce fighting of the Totenkopf", Eicke was awarded Oak Leaves to the Knight's Cross on 20 May _____
Waffen-SS.fact: "For his excellence in command and the particularly fierce fighting of the Totenkopf", Eicke was awarded Oak Leaves to the Knight's Cross on 20 May 1942.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: They were followed in July by the 11th SS _____ created from Norwegian and Danish volunteers
Waffen-SS.fact: They were followed in July by the 11th SS Volunteer Panzergrenadier Division Nordland created from Norwegian and Danish volunteers.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: September saw the formation of the 12th SS _____ using volunteers from the Hitler Youth
Waffen-SS.fact: September saw the formation of the 12th SS Panzer Division Hitlerjugend using volunteers from the Hitler Youth.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: The 12th SS _____ had lost 94 per cent of its armour, nearly all of its artillery, and 70 per cent of its vehicles
Waffen-SS.fact: September saw the formation of the 12th SS Panzer Division Hitlerjugend using volunteers from the Hitler Youth.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: This was followed by the 14th _____ of the SS (1st Galician) formed from volunteers from Galicia in western Ukraine
Waffen-SS.fact: This was followed by the 14th Waffen Grenadier Division of the SS (1st Galician) formed from volunteers from Galicia in western Ukraine. The 15th Waffen Grenadier Division of the SS (1st Latvian) was created in 1943, using compulsory military service in the Ostland.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: The 15th Waffen Grenadier Division of the SS (1st Latvian) was created in _____, using compulsory military service in the Ostland
Waffen-SS.fact: The 15th Waffen Grenadier Division of the SS (1st Latvian) was created in 1943, using compulsory military service in the Ostland. The final new division of 1943 was the 16th SS Panzergrenadier Division Reichsführer-SS, which was created using the Sturmbrigade Reichsführer SS as a cadre.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: The final new division of _____ was the 16th SS Panzergrenadier Division Reichsführer-SS, which was created using the Sturmbrigade Reichsführer SS as a cadre
Waffen-SS.fact: The 15th Waffen Grenadier Division of the SS (1st Latvian) was created in 1943, using compulsory military service in the Ostland. The final new division of 1943 was the 16th SS Panzergrenadier Division Reichsführer-SS, which was created using the Sturmbrigade Reichsführer SS as a cadre.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: By _____ the Waffen-SS could no longer claim to be an "elite" fighting force
Waffen-SS.fact: The 15th Waffen Grenadier Division of the SS (1st Latvian) was created in 1943, using compulsory military service in the Ostland. The final new division of 1943 was the 16th SS Panzergrenadier Division Reichsführer-SS, which was created using the Sturmbrigade Reichsführer SS as a cadre.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: Hitler ordered the SS _____ back to the Eastern Front for a counter-attack with the city of Kharkov as its objective
Waffen-SS.fact: Hitler ordered the SS Panzer Corps back to the Eastern Front for a counter-attack with the city of Kharkov as its objective. The SS Panzer Corps was in full retreat on 19 February, having been attacked by the Soviet 6th Army, when they received the order to counter-attack.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: The SS _____ was in full retreat on 19 February, having been attacked by the Soviet 6th Army, when they received the order to counter-attack
Waffen-SS.fact: Hitler ordered the SS Panzer Corps back to the Eastern Front for a counter-attack with the city of Kharkov as its objective. The SS Panzer Corps was in full retreat on 19 February, having been attacked by the Soviet 6th Army, when they received the order to counter-attack.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: Despite orders to encircle _____ from the north, the SS Panzer Corps directly attacked in the Third Battle of Kharkov on 11 March
Waffen-SS.fact: During Field Marshal Erich von Manstein's counteroffensive, the SS Panzer Corps, without support from the Luftwaffe or neighbouring German formations, broke through the Soviet line and advanced on Kharkov. Despite orders to encircle Kharkov from the north, the SS Panzer Corps directly attacked in the Third Battle of Kharkov on 11 March.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: This led to four days of house-to-house fighting before Kharkov was recaptured by the _____ on 15 March
Waffen-SS.fact: This led to four days of house-to-house fighting before Kharkov was recaptured by the Leibstandarte Division on 15 March.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: Two days later, the Germans recaptured Belgorod, creating the salient that, in July _____, led to the Battle of Kursk
Waffen-SS.fact: Two days later, the Germans recaptured Belgorod, creating the salient that, in July 1943, led to the Battle of Kursk.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: The II SS _____ spearheaded the attack through the Soviet defences
Waffen-SS.fact: The German offensive cost the Red Army an estimated 70,000 casualties but the house-to-house fighting in Kharkov was particularly bloody for the SS Panzer Corps, which lost approximately 44% of its strength by the time operations ended in late March. The II SS Panzer Corps spearheaded the attack through the Soviet defences.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: The attack penetrated to a depth of _____ (22 mi) and was then stopped by the Soviet 1st Tank Army
Waffen-SS.fact: The attack penetrated to a depth of 35 kilometres (22 mi) and was then stopped by the Soviet 1st Tank Army.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: The Soviet reserves had been sent south to defend against a German attack by the III _____
Waffen-SS.fact: The II SS Panzer Corps spearheaded the attack through the Soviet defences. The Soviet reserves had been sent south to defend against a German attack by the III Panzer Corps.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: With the loss of their reserves, any hope they may have had of dealing a major defeat to the II SS _____ ended
Waffen-SS.fact: The II SS Panzer Corps spearheaded the attack through the Soviet defences. The Soviet reserves had been sent south to defend against a German attack by the III Panzer Corps.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: But the _____ advances now failed – despite appalling losses, the Soviet tank armies held the line and prevented the II SS Panzer Corps from making the expected breakthrough
Waffen-SS.fact: The Soviet reserves had been sent south to defend against a German attack by the III Panzer Corps. But the German advances now failed – despite appalling losses, the Soviet tank armies held the line and prevented the II SS Panzer Corps from making the expected breakthrough.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: A parallel attack by the _____ against the new 6th Army on the Mius river south of Kharkov necessitated the withdrawal of reserve forces held to exploit any success on the southern shoulder of Kursk
Waffen-SS.fact: A parallel attack by the Red Army against the new 6th Army on the Mius river south of Kharkov necessitated the withdrawal of reserve forces held to exploit any success on the southern shoulder of Kursk. The Soviet Union was not beaten, and the strategic initiative had swung to the Red Army.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: The Soviet Union was not beaten, and the strategic initiative had swung to the _____
Waffen-SS.fact: A parallel attack by the Red Army against the new 6th Army on the Mius river south of Kharkov necessitated the withdrawal of reserve forces held to exploit any success on the southern shoulder of Kursk. The Soviet Union was not beaten, and the strategic initiative had swung to the Red Army.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: The OKW also had to draw on some German troops from the _____ to bolster the Mediterranean theatre following the Allied invasion of Sicily
Waffen-SS.fact: The OKW also had to draw on some German troops from the Eastern Front to bolster the Mediterranean theatre following the Allied invasion of Sicily.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: On 17 July, _____ called off the operation and ordered a withdrawal
Waffen-SS.fact: The failure to break through the Soviet tactical zone and the need to break off the assault by the German 9th Army on the northern shoulder of the Kursk salient due to Operation Kutuzov contributed to Hitler's decision to halt the offensive. On 17 July, Hitler called off the operation and ordered a withdrawal.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: The Germans were forced onto the defensive as the _____ began the liberation of Western Russia
Waffen-SS.fact: The Soviet Union was not beaten, and the strategic initiative had swung to the Red Army. The Germans were forced onto the defensive as the Red Army began the liberation of Western Russia.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: The division left behind its armour and equipment, which was given to the _____ and Totenkopf Divisions
Waffen-SS.fact: The division left behind its armour and equipment, which was given to the Das Reich and Totenkopf Divisions.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: After the Italian surrender and collapse of 8 September _____, the Leibstandarte was ordered to begin disarming nearby Italian units
Waffen-SS.fact: After the Italian surrender and collapse of 8 September 1943, the Leibstandarte was ordered to begin disarming nearby Italian units.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: It also had the task of guarding vital road and rail junctions in the north of _____ and was involved in several skirmishes with partisans
Waffen-SS.fact: It also had the task of guarding vital road and rail junctions in the north of Italy and was involved in several skirmishes with partisans.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: This went smoothly, with the exception of a brief skirmish with _____ troops stationed in Parma on 9 September
Waffen-SS.fact: After the Italian surrender and collapse of 8 September 1943, the Leibstandarte was ordered to begin disarming nearby Italian units. This went smoothly, with the exception of a brief skirmish with Italian troops stationed in Parma on 9 September.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: By 19 _____, all Italian forces in the Po River plain had been disarmed, but the OKW received reports that elements of the Italian 4th Army were regrouping in Piedmont, near the French border
Waffen-SS.fact: After the Italian surrender and collapse of 8 September 1943, the Leibstandarte was ordered to begin disarming nearby Italian units. This went smoothly, with the exception of a brief skirmish with Italian troops stationed in Parma on 9 September.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: On arriving in the province of Cuneo, Peiper was met by an _____ officer who warned that his forces would attack unless Peiper's unit vacated the province immediately
Waffen-SS.fact: This went smoothly, with the exception of a brief skirmish with Italian troops stationed in Parma on 9 September. By 19 September, all Italian forces in the Po River plain had been disarmed, but the OKW received reports that elements of the Italian 4th Army were regrouping in Piedmont, near the French border.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: After Peiper refused, the _____ attacked

Waffen-SS.fact: As a part of Operation Konrad I, the IV SS Panzer Corps was committed to action on 1 January 1945, near Tata, with the advance columns of the Wiking Division slamming into the Soviet 4th Guards Army.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: A heavy battle ensued, with the Wiking and _____ destroying many of the Soviet tanks
Waffen-SS.fact: A heavy battle ensued, with the Wiking and Totenkopf Division destroying many of the Soviet tanks.

Waffen-SS.fact: The Red Army manoeuvred forces to block the advance, halting them at Bicske, 28 km (17 mi) from Budapest.

Waffen-SS.fact: The siege lasted from 29 December 1944 until the city surrendered unconditionally on 13 February 1945.

Waffen-SS.fact: January saw the 32nd SS Volunteer Grenadier Division 30 Januar formed from the remnants of other units and staff from the SS Junker Schools. The SS Volunteer Grenadier Brigade Landstorm Nederland was upgraded to the 34th SS Volunteer Grenadier Division Landstorm Nederland.

Waffen-SS.fact: In February, the Waffen Grenadier Brigade of the SS Charlemagne was upgraded to a division and became called the 33rd Waffen Grenadier Division of the SS Charlemagne (1st French).

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: The SS _____ was upgraded to the 34th SS Volunteer Grenadier Division Landstorm Nederland
Waffen-SS.fact: The SS Volunteer Grenadier Brigade Landstorm Nederland was upgraded to the 34th SS Volunteer Grenadier Division Landstorm Nederland.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences

Waffen-SS.fact: The second SS police division followed when the 35th SS-Police Grenadier Division was formed from SS police units that had been transferred to the Waffen-SS.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: The third SS cavalry division, the 37th SS _____, was formed from the remnants of the 8th and 22nd SS Cavalry Divisions, which had both been virtually destroyed
Waffen-SS.fact: The third SS cavalry division, the 37th SS Volunteer Cavalry Division, was formed from the remnants of the 8th and 22nd SS Cavalry Divisions, which had both been virtually destroyed.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: It began on 1 January _____ in Alsace and Lorraine in northeastern France, and it ended on 25 January
Waffen-SS.fact: It began on 1 January 1945 in Alsace and Lorraine in northeastern France, and it ended on 25 January.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: The initial attack was conducted by three corps of the 1st _____
Waffen-SS.fact: The initial attack was conducted by three corps of the 1st Army. By 15 January, at least 17 German divisions (including units in the Colmar Pocket) were engaged, including the XIII SS Army Corps (the 17th and 38th SS Divisions) and the 6th and 10th SS Panzer Divisions.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: At the same time, the _____ mounted a large offensive over the skies of France
Waffen-SS.fact: At the same time, the Luftwaffe mounted a large offensive over the skies of France. It was the 'last gasp' attempt for the Luftwaffe to take back air supremacy from the Western Allies.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: It was the 'last gasp' attempt for the _____ to take back air supremacy from the Western Allies
Waffen-SS.fact: At the same time, the Luftwaffe mounted a large offensive over the skies of France. It was the 'last gasp' attempt for the Luftwaffe to take back air supremacy from the Western Allies.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: It was a limited counterattack by the three Corps of the 11th SS _____, which was being assembled in Pomerania, against the spearheads of the Soviet 1st Belorussian Front
Waffen-SS.fact: It was a limited counterattack by the three Corps of the 11th SS Panzer Army, which was being assembled in Pomerania, against the spearheads of the Soviet 1st Belorussian Front.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: It was repulsed by the _____, but helped to convince the Soviet High Command to postpone the planned attack on Berlin
Waffen-SS.fact: It was repulsed by the Red Army, but helped to convince the Soviet High Command to postpone the planned attack on Berlin.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: Initially, the attack achieved a total surprise, reaching the banks of the _____ and, on 17 January, Arnswalde
Waffen-SS.fact: Initially, the attack achieved a total surprise, reaching the banks of the Ina River and, on 17 January, Arnswalde.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences

Waffen-SS.fact: The III (Germanic) SS Panzer Corps was pulled back to Stargard and Stettin on the northern Oder River. The Waffen-SS units involved were the 11th SS Nordland, 20th SS Estonian, 23rd SS Nederland, 27th SS Langemark, and 28th SS Wallonien Divisions all in the III (Germanic) SS Panzer Corps and the X SS Corps, which did not command any SS units.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: In March _____, the X SS Corps was encircled by the 1st Guards Tank Army, 3rd Shock Army, and First Polish Army in the area of Dramburg
Waffen-SS.fact: In March 1945, the X SS Corps was encircled by the 1st Guards Tank Army, 3rd Shock Army, and First Polish Army in the area of Dramburg. This pocket was destroyed by the Red Army on 7 March 1945.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: This pocket was destroyed by the Red Army on 7 March _____
Waffen-SS.fact: In March 1945, the X SS Corps was encircled by the 1st Guards Tank Army, 3rd Shock Army, and First Polish Army in the area of Dramburg. This pocket was destroyed by the Red Army on 7 March 1945.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: On 8 March _____, the Soviets announced the capture of General Krappe and 8,000 men of the corps
Waffen-SS.fact: In March 1945, the X SS Corps was encircled by the 1st Guards Tank Army, 3rd Shock Army, and First Polish Army in the area of Dramburg. This pocket was destroyed by the Red Army on 7 March 1945.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: The SS divisions were pulled out and refitted in Germany in preparation for _____ (Frühlingserwachsen)
Waffen-SS.fact: The SS divisions were pulled out and refitted in Germany in preparation for Operation Spring Awakening (Frühlingserwachsen).

Waffen-SS.fact: Hitler ordered Dietrich's 6th Panzer Army to take the lead and move to Hungary in order to protect the oilfields and refineries there.

Waffen-SS.question: The 6th _____ was made up of the I SS Panzer Corps (the 1st and 12th SS Panzer Divisions) and the II SS Panzer Corps (the 2nd and 10th SS Panzer Divisions)
Waffen-SS.fact: Hitler ordered Dietrich's 6th Panzer Army to take the lead and move to Hungary in order to protect the oilfields and refineries there. The 6th Panzer Army was made up of the I SS Panzer Corps (the 1st and 12th SS Panzer Divisions) and the II SS Panzer Corps (the 2nd and 10th SS Panzer Divisions).

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences

Waffen-SS.fact: Hitler ordered Dietrich's 6th Panzer Army to take the lead and move to Hungary in order to protect the oilfields and refineries there. The 6th Panzer Army was made up of the I SS Panzer Corps (the 1st and 12th SS Panzer Divisions) and the II SS Panzer Corps (the 2nd and 10th SS Panzer Divisions).

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: This final _____ offensive in the east began on 6 March
Waffen-SS.fact: This final German offensive in the east began on 6 March. The German forces attacked near Lake Balaton with the 6th Panzer Army advancing northwards towards Budapest and the 2nd Panzer Army moving eastwards and south.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: The German forces attacked near _____ with the 6th Panzer Army advancing northwards towards Budapest and the 2nd Panzer Army moving eastwards and south
Waffen-SS.fact: The German forces attacked near Lake Balaton with the 6th Panzer Army advancing northwards towards Budapest and the 2nd Panzer Army moving eastwards and south.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: The overwhelming numerical superiority of the _____ made any defence impossible, yet Hitler somehow had believed victory was attainable
Waffen-SS.fact: The overwhelming numerical superiority of the Red Army made any defence impossible, yet Hitler somehow had believed victory was attainable. The only major force to face the attacking Red Army was the II SS Panzer Corps (the 2nd and 3rd SS Panzer Divisions), under the command of Wilhelm Bittrich, along with ad hoc forces made up of garrison and anti-aircraft units.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: After Operation Spring Awakening, the 6th _____ withdrew towards Vienna and was involved what became known as the Vienna Offensive
Waffen-SS.fact: The German forces attacked near Lake Balaton with the 6th Panzer Army advancing northwards towards Budapest and the 2nd Panzer Army moving eastwards and south. After Operation Spring Awakening, the 6th Panzer Army withdrew towards Vienna and was involved what became called the Vienna Offensive.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: Vienna fell to the _____ on 13 April
Waffen-SS.fact: Vienna fell to the Soviets on 13 April.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: Bittrich's II SS _____ had pulled out to the west that evening to avoid encirclement
Waffen-SS.fact: The only major force to face the attacking Red Army was the II SS Panzer Corps (the 2nd and 3rd SS Panzer Divisions), under the command of Wilhelm Bittrich, along with ad hoc forces made up of garrison and anti-aircraft units. Bittrich's II SS Panzer Corps had pulled out to the west that evening to avoid encirclement.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: The _____ retreated westward with less than 1,600 men and 16 tanks remaining
Waffen-SS.fact: The LSSAH retreated westward with less than 1,600 men and 16 tanks remaining.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: The order was issued to _____ by Hitler, who claimed that the troops, and more importantly, the 1st SS Division Leibstandarte, "did not fight as the situation demanded"
Waffen-SS.fact: The order was issued to Dietrich by Hitler, who claimed that the troops, and more importantly, the 1st SS Division Leibstandarte, "did not fight as the situation demanded". Dietrich did not relay the order to his troops.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: It fought in the _____ of the Seelow Heights (16–19 April) and the Battle of Halbe (21 April – 1 May), both part of the Battle of Berlin
Waffen-SS.fact: As a mark of disgrace, the Waffen-SS units involved in the battle were ordered to remove their distinctive cuff titles. It fought in the Battle of the Seelow Heights (16–19 April) and the Battle of Halbe (21 April – 1 May), both part of the Battle of Berlin.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: On 23 April, SS-_____ührer Wilhelm Mohnke was appointed by Hitler as Battle Commander for the centre government district (Zitadelle sector), which included the Reich Chancellery and the Führerbunker
Waffen-SS.fact: On 23 April, SS-Brigadeführer Wilhelm Mohnke was appointed by Hitler as Battle Commander for the centre government district (Zitadelle sector), which included the Reich Chancellery and the Führerbunker.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: He formed _____, divided into two weak regiments
Waffen-SS.fact: He formed Kampfgruppe Mohnke, divided into two weak regiments.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: On 23 April, the _____ ordered SS-Brigadeführer Gustav Krukenberg to proceed to Berlin with his men, who were reorganised as Assault Battalion Charlemagne
Waffen-SS.fact: Mohnke's command post was in the bunkers under the Reich Chancellery. On 23 April, the Reich Chancellery ordered SS-Brigadeführer Gustav Krukenberg to proceed to Berlin with his men, who were reorganised as Assault Battalion Charlemagne.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: Between 320 and 330 _____ troops arrived in Berlin on 24 April after a long detour to avoid Soviet advance columns
Waffen-SS.fact: Between 320 and 330 French troops arrived in Berlin on 24 April after a long detour to avoid Soviet advance columns.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: Krukenberg was also appointed the commander of (Berlin) _____ included the Nordland Division, whose previous commander, Joachim Ziegler, was relieved of command the same day
Waffen-SS.fact: Krukenberg was also appointed the commander of (Berlin) Defence Sector C. This included the Nordland Division, whose previous commander, Joachim Ziegler, was relieved of command the same day.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: The men of the _____ were now under Mohnke's overall command
Waffen-SS.fact: Krukenberg was also appointed the commander of (Berlin) Defence Sector C. This included the Nordland Division, whose previous commander, Joachim Ziegler, was relieved of command the same day. The men of the Nordland Division were now under Mohnke's overall command.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: A heavy artillery bombardment of the centre government district had begun on 20 April _____ and lasted until the end of hostilities
Waffen-SS.fact: A heavy artillery bombardment of the centre government district had begun on 20 April 1945 and lasted until the end of hostilities.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: Under intense shelling, the SS troops put up stiff resistance which led to bitter and bloody street fighting with the _____
Waffen-SS.fact: Under intense shelling, the SS troops put up stiff resistance which led to bitter and bloody street fighting with the Red Army.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: By 26 April, the defenders were pushed back into the Reichstag and _____
Waffen-SS.fact: By 26 April, the defenders were pushed back into the Reichstag and Reich Chancellery.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: There, over the next few days, the survivors (mainly French SS troops from the former 33rd SS _____) fought in vain against the Soviets
Waffen-SS.fact: There, over the next few days, the survivors (mainly French SS troops from the former 33rd SS Division Charlemagne) fought in vain against the Soviets.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: Prior to the break-out, _____ briefed all commanders that could be reached within the Zitadelle sector about Hitler's death and the planned break-out
Waffen-SS.fact: Prior to the break-out, Mohnke briefed all commanders that could be reached within the Zitadelle sector about Hitler's death and the planned break-out.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: There were ten main groups that attempted to head northwest towards _____
Waffen-SS.fact: There were ten main groups that attempted to head northwest towards Mecklenburg.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: What was left of the _____ under Krukenberg fought hard in that area, but Soviet artillery, anti-tank guns, and tanks destroyed the groups
Waffen-SS.fact: What was left of the Nordland Division under Krukenberg fought hard in that area, but Soviet artillery, anti-tank guns, and tanks destroyed the groups.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: Several very small groups managed to reach the _____ at the Elbe's west bank, but most, including Mohnke's group, could not make it through the Soviet rings
Waffen-SS.fact: Several very small groups managed to reach the Americans at the Elbe's west bank, but most, including Mohnke's group, could not make it through the Soviet rings.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: Using a forged paybook under the name of _____, he fled south on 11 May to Friedrichskoog
Waffen-SS.fact: Using a forged paybook under the name of Sergeant Heinrich Hitzinger, he fled south on 11 May to Friedrichskoog.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: On 21 May, _____ and two aides were detained at a checkpoint set up by former Soviet POWs and then handed over to the British Army
Waffen-SS.fact: Himmler fled and attempted to go into hiding. On 21 May, Himmler and two aides were detained at a checkpoint set up by former Soviet POWs and then handed over to the British Army.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: On 23 May, after _____ had admitted his real identity, a doctor attempted to examine him
Waffen-SS.fact: Himmler fled and attempted to go into hiding. On 21 May, Himmler and two aides were detained at a checkpoint set up by former Soviet POWs and then handed over to the British Army.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: However, _____ bit into a hidden cyanide pill and collapsed onto the floor
Waffen-SS.fact: On 21 May, Himmler and two aides were detained at a checkpoint set up by former Soviet POWs and then handed over to the British Army. On 23 May, after Himmler had admitted his real identity, a doctor attempted to examine him.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: A total of 39 were formed, beginning with the initial three in _____ and ramping up to nine alone in 1945
Waffen-SS.fact: A total of 39 were formed, beginning with the initial three in 1933 and ramping up to nine alone in 1945.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: Many of the late-formed higher-numbered units were in fact small battlegroups (_____), and divisions in name only
Waffen-SS.fact: Many of the late-formed higher-numbered units were in fact small battlegroups (Kampfgruppen), and divisions in name only.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: He would command the _____ SS Adolf Hitler from its inception to regiment, brigade, and division
Waffen-SS.fact: He would command the Leibstandarte SS Adolf Hitler from its inception to regiment, brigade, and division.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: He was then given command of the I SS _____ and by the end of the war was the commander of the 6th Panzer Army
Waffen-SS.fact: He was then given command of the I SS Panzer Corps and by the end of the war was the commander of the 6th Panzer Army. He went on to command the II SS Panzer Corps and the 7th Army.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: He went on to command the II SS _____ and the 7th Army
Waffen-SS.fact: He was then given command of the I SS Panzer Corps and by the end of the war was the commander of the 6th Panzer Army. He went on to command the II SS Panzer Corps and the 7th Army.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: Paul Hausser, a former general in the regular army, was chosen by _____ to transform the SS-VT into a credible military organisation
Waffen-SS.fact: Paul Hausser, a former general in the regular army, was chosen by Himmler to transform the SS-VT into a credible military organisation.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: Casualty rates were not significantly higher than in the _____ overall and were comparable to those among the armoured divisions of the army and the Luftwaffe paratroop formations
Waffen-SS.fact: Casualty rates were not significantly higher than in the Wehrmacht overall and were comparable to those among the armoured divisions of the army and the Luftwaffe paratroop formations.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: A number of SS medical personnel who were members of the Waffen-SS were convicted of crimes during the "Doctors' trials" in Nuremberg, held between _____ and 1947 for the Nazi human experimentation th
Waffen-SS.fact: A number of SS medical personnel who were members of the Waffen-SS were convicted of crimes during the "Doctors' trials" in Nuremberg, held between 1946 and 1947 for the Nazi human experimentation they performed at the camps.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: After the war the SS organisation as a whole was held to be a criminal organisation by the post-war _____ government
Waffen-SS.fact: After the war the SS organisation as a whole was held to be a criminal organisation by the post-war German government.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: Their leader, _____, who was the commandant of Dachau, inspector of the camps, and murderer of Ernst Röhm, later became the commander of the 3rd SS Totenkopf Division
Waffen-SS.fact: After the war the SS organisation as a whole was held to be a criminal organisation by the post-war German government. Formations such as the Dirlewanger and Kaminski Brigades were singled out, and many others participated in large-scale massacres or smaller-scale killings such as murder of 34 captured allied servicemen ordered by Josef Kieffer during Operation Bulbasket in 1944, the Houtman affair, or murders perpetrated by Heinrich Boere.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: With the invasion of _____, the Totenkopfverbände troops were called on to carry out so-called "police and security measures" in rear areas
Waffen-SS.fact: The listed Waffen-SS units were responsible for the following massacres: Wormhoudt massacre by the SS Leibstandarte Adolf Hitler, 1940, France Le Paradis massacre by the SS Division Totenkopf, 1940, France Pripyat swamps (punitive operation) by the SS Cavalry Brigade, 1941, USSR Ascq massacre by the 12th SS Panzer Division Hitlerjugend, 1944, France Tulle massacre by 2nd SS Panzer Division Das Reich, 1944, France Oradour-sur-Glane massacre by the 2nd SS Panzer Division Das Reich, 1944, France...

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: What these measures entailed is demonstrated by the record of _____
Waffen-SS.fact: The listed Waffen-SS units were responsible for the following massacres: Wormhoudt massacre by the SS Leibstandarte Adolf Hitler, 1940, France Le Paradis massacre by the SS Division Totenkopf, 1940, France Pripyat swamps (punitive operation) by the SS Cavalry Brigade, 1941, USSR Ascq massacre by the 12th SS Panzer Division Hitlerjugend, 1944, France Tulle massacre by 2nd SS Panzer Division Das Reich, 1944, France Oradour-sur-Glane massacre by the 2nd SS Panzer Division Das Reich, 1944, France...

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: Approximately 800 _____ civilians and what the Sicherheitsdienst (SD) termed "potential resistance leaders" were killed
Waffen-SS.fact: Approximately 800 Polish civilians and what the Sicherheitsdienst (SD) termed "potential resistance leaders" were killed.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: Later the formation became the _____rd SS Panzer Division Totenkopf, but from the start they were among the first executors of a policy of systematic extermination
Waffen-SS.fact: It arrived in Włocławek on 22 September 1939 and embarked on a four-day "Jewish action" that included the burning of synagogues and the execution en masse of the leaders of the Jewish community. Later the formation became the 3rd SS Panzer Division Totenkopf, but from the start they were among the first executors of a policy of systematic extermination.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: The end of the war saw a number of war crime trials, including the _____ massacre trial
Waffen-SS.fact: The end of the war saw a number of war crime trials, including the Malmedy massacre trial. The counts of indictment related to the massacre of more than 300 American prisoners in the vicinity of Malmedy, between 16 December 1944 and 13 January 1945, and the massacre of 100 Belgian civilians mainly in the vicinity of Stavelot.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: The counts of indictment related to the massacre of more than 300 American prisoners in the vicinity of Malmedy, between 16 December _____ and 13 January 1945, and the massacre of 100 Belgian civilian
Waffen-SS.fact: The counts of indictment related to the massacre of more than 300 American prisoners in the vicinity of Malmedy, between 16 December 1944 and 13 January 1945, and the massacre of 100 Belgian civilians mainly in the vicinity of Stavelot.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: In _____, the Polish parliament classified the crimes of the 14th Grenadier Division's soldiers against the Polish population as genocide
Waffen-SS.fact: In 2016, the Polish parliament classified the crimes of the 14th Grenadier Division's soldiers against the Polish population as genocide.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: SS-Gruppenführer Heinz Lammerding, who commanded the Das Reich Division that perpetrated the Tulle and the Oradour-sur-Glane massacres in occupied France, died in _____, following a successful busines
Waffen-SS.fact: SS-Gruppenführer Heinz Lammerding, who commanded the Das Reich Division that perpetrated the Tulle and the Oradour-sur-Glane massacres in occupied France, died in 1971, following a successful business career in West Germany.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: The West German government refused to extradite him to France since, as originally drafted, Article 16(2) of the _____ did not permit German citizens to be extradited to foreign countries
Waffen-SS.fact: The West German government refused to extradite him to France since, as originally drafted, Article 16(2) of the German Basic Law did not permit German citizens to be extradited to foreign countries.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: Extradition requests from Italy were rejected by Germany, even though the German Basic Law had been amended after _____ to permit the extradition of German citizens to member states of the European Un
Waffen-SS.fact: Extradition requests from Italy were rejected by Germany, even though the German Basic Law had been amended after 2000 to permit the extradition of German citizens to member states of the European Union.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: Kurt Meyer, _____ührer of the 12th SS Division, a convicted war criminal, was HIAG's most effective spokesperson
Waffen-SS.fact: Kurt Meyer, Brigadeführer of the 12th SS Division, a convicted war criminal, was HIAG's most effective spokesperson.

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: Always in touch with its Nazi past, HIAG was a subject of significant controversy, both in _____ and abroad, since its founding

Waffen-SS.subject: Applied Sciences
Waffen-SS.question: It was disbanded in _____ at the federal level, but local groups, along with the organisation's monthly periodical, continued to exist at least into the 2000s
